title: Run of a composed machine
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, with state sets $S_1$ and $S_2$, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. Form a machine on $S_1\sqcup S_2$ that follows $M_1$ on left states, switches from the specified exit state to the specified entry state in one step without changing the tapes, and follows $M_2$ on right states. If $M_1$ takes the initial configuration with state $start$ and work tapes $w_0$ to the configuration with state $exit$ and work tapes $w_1$ after $T_1$ steps, never having state $exit$ earlier, and $M_2$ takes the initial configuration with state $entry$ and work tapes $w_1$ to the configuration with state $q_2$ and work tapes $w_2$ after $T_2$ steps, then the composed machine takes the initial configuration with state $(left,start)$ and work tapes $w_0$ to the configuration with state $(right,q_2)$ and work tapes $w_2$ after $T_1+1+T_2$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M_1,M_2$ are machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet
$M_1$ reaches the configuration $(exit,w_1)$ from $(start,w_0)$ in $T_1$ steps
$M_1$ does not have state $exit$ at any earlier time $t<T_1$
